newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees peaceful conclusion to hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees peaceful conclusion to hostage crisis.

text.p: In its first public statement since the start of the hostage crisis, the Peruvian government said on Friday it was confident of a peaceful solution to the siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Worldwide support for Peru gave the government "the peace and strength of mind to trust that we will reach a peaceful solution," Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi said.

The government has so far maintained a hard line with the guerrillas, who are threatening to kill about 400 hostages held at the Japanese ambassador's residence, by refusing to meet their demand to release up to 500 jailed comrades.

But the government had the will "to preserve the lives of everybody at the site," Pandolfi said, adding the assault was "an isolated act that in no way affects the security or stability of our country."
The rebels have not spoken directly to government officials but, rather, have been channelling information to authorities outside the compound through released diplomats and Red Cross officials.
